topics.topic: How AuditEntry identity and sequence numbers are scoped across restored store histories
questions: Is a store history merely an implicit scope, making an AuditEntry identity the sequence number within the currently installed history, or must Registry mint and retain a history identity so entries from pre-loss and post-restore histories remain distinguishable?

Are audit entries in the backup the same entities continued into the new history or new history-local entities, and may sequence numbers used after the backup in the lost history be reused by different entries after restoration?

quotes: its sequence number, minted by Registry: 1 for the store's first entry, then one more than the last its store's history ever wrote; never reused within that history, also after old entries are erased (R0-66), so the log's order is the order of the numbers even where two entries share an instant (owner, 2026-10-31; codex round-02 T2). A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number (R0-89);
judgement.why: AuditEntry sequence identity is explicitly scoped to one store history, and a restored history continues from the backup's last number, allowing numbers from the lost post-backup tail to be used in the new history without requiring a stored history identity.

topics.topic: Whether restored AgentSession access state reverts exactly to the backup
questions: If a backup predates a revocation, project erasure, active-project change or grant, does the restored AgentSession access exactly revert to the backup, including restoring a grant and permitting later operations that the lost history had revoked?
Can restoring an older backup reinstate a revoked grant or active project, remove a later grant, or restore an earlier pending access request and access version?

quotes: A backup holds every record but the agent sessions (M06): a store restored from it has no session, Kernel registers its sessions again and the owner grants them again, so a restore never brings back a grant revoked after the backup.
A store restored from a backup holds no agent session.
A tested restore exists every day without a second instance holding production data (R0-34); a restore cannot revive a revoked grant.
judgement.why: State 2 decides that AgentSession records are excluded from backups, so no grant, active project, pending request, or access version is restored.

topics.topic: Whether restoring an older backup can roll back domain-record lifecycle and persistence outcomes
questions: Are these lifecycle and persistence guarantees scoped only to one store history, so restoring an older backup may resurrect earlier model states or remove models created later?

Are those lifecycle guarantees final only within one store history, so restoring an older backup may make an archived project active again, restore an anonymised or deleted project, remove rooms added later, or restore an earlier pointer status?
May restoration from a pre-erasure backup make an erased Customer live again, restore removed personal data, or undo restriction, lifting, ending or resumption marks?

quotes: A backup holds every record but the agent sessions (M06): a store restored from it has no session, Kernel registers its sessions again and the owner grants them again, so a restore never brings back a grant revoked after the backup.
While the daily runs succeed, an erasure reaches the backups at most 30 days after it, and a restore loses at most a day of changes; a failed run lengthens both by the days until a run succeeds.

Registry has no restore operation (R0-89). A store the owner puts in place of a lost one starts as any store (A17 rule 5) — by the release that made its backup, or by a later one after that release's own store migration — and begins its own history from the backup: numbering continues from its last number (A15), and a store without the migration closure accepts the import (A16).
judgement.why: State 2 says the backup contains every non-session record and that restoration loses post-backup changes, so domain records and lifecycle facts return to the state captured by that backup within the new store history.

topics.topic: Whether backup restoration can resurrect erased AuditEntry records
questions: May restoring a backup made before an audit erasure make the erased AuditEntry records readable again in the new store history?

topics.topic: Whether restored domain records retain their original identities or become new history-local entities
questions: Does a restored Project, Customer, Room, ArtifactPointer or AgentSession retain the identity of the record represented in the backup, or does the new store history contain distinct entities that reuse those identifiers?
